title: Which loop order, and why

prereqs.why: The answer is which index walks contiguously in C's layout.
The cost difference is entirely about how much of each fetched line gets used.

hints: In C, `a[i][j]` and `a[i][j+1]` are next to each other in memory. What about `a[i][j]` and `a[i+1][j]`?
A 64-byte line holds eight doubles. Work out how many of those eight each version uses before moving on.
The factor of eight in the measurement and the number of doubles per line are the same number. That is not a coincidence.

options: Version A walks memory contiguously, so each 64-byte line it fetches supplies eight consecutive additions. Version B strides by a whole row, so each fetched line supplies one addition and the other seven doubles are wasted.
Version A performs fewer additions, because the inner loop over `j` can be vectorised while the inner loop over `i` cannot.
Version B is slower because it causes more TLB misses, and the cache behaviour of the two is the same.
Version B accesses the array out of bounds on the last iteration, and the slowdown is the cost of the resulting page faults.
